## One list, several definitions of a purchase

Choose a cleaning or counting rule. The chart shows how many customers **enter** or **leave** the contact list relative to the reference pipeline. The list uses the module's fixed decision: contact a customer when 10% assumed revenue lift at 30% gross margin exceeds a £10 contact cost. The bars are measured changes from the module's full run, not a live model refit.

**Work one example.** Counting invoices instead of purchase days adds 14 customers and drops 139, so the list falls from 2,212 to 2,087. It changes frequency even when a customer splits one basket across two invoices on the same day. Customer 12346 is a sharper example in the [module](../modules/13-messy-real-data.qmd): after excluding test lines and a cancelled bulk order, their projected revenue falls below the contact threshold.

**Data.** The contact-list counts were computed in the module's full run on [UCI Online Retail II](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/502/online+retail+ii), a real transaction dataset. UCI's dataset description and CC BY 4.0 license were verified 2026-10-27. The modules' run record, cleaning definitions, and customer-level explanation remain the source of the measured numbers. The lift, margin, and cost are scenario assumptions.
